target_customer: Businesses (banks, retailers, fintechs, apps) in Latin America that want to offer bill pay and payments
problem: Paying bills and services in Latin America was fragmented; businesses needed one API to offer payments across countries.
business_model: Payments-as-a-service API, per-transaction fees (assumed from category; not sourced)

founders.name: Edrizio De La Cruz
founders.background_notes: Former YC Visiting Partner per YC page.

founders.name: Iñigo Rumayor
previous_startups: Regalii (cross-border bill pay; CRO and COO)

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with many LatAm billers, banks and payment rails; compliance and integration work rather than research. Rated from category, no detailed source read.

defensibility.rationale: Biller integrations and bank relationships in several countries are hard to copy quickly, but this is an inference not stated by a source.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mastercard announced it would acquire Arcus on 2021-12-03 per YC page; described as its first LatAm acquisition. Price not found.

market_need_then: Latin America had large unbanked and underbanked populations paying bills in cash; the YC description names clients BBVA, Santander, Walmart, 7-Eleven and Rappi, which shows demand later, not at founding.

brand_strength.rationale: Name origin not found in sources read.

outcome_analysis: Arcus grew from a 2013 Summer batch company into a LatAm payments platform serving large banks and retailers, backed by a16z, SoftBank, Citi Ventures and Initialized among others, and was acquired by Mastercard in December 2021 after about eight years. The sale price is not public in sources read, and round sizes were not verified, so the exit scale is unknown; a strategic acquirer buying a regional infrastructure layer is consistent with the integration-heavy moat.
notes: Investors listed from YC page and long description; no round amounts verified, so rounds left empty and coverage partial. Mastercard press release returned 403 and was not worked around.
